answer:
No. Your records show you were checked for a blood clot in the lung, and the scan found none.

On 8 July 2025, at Cascade North Demo Hospital, you had a D-dimer blood test. It came back raised at 0.92 mg/L (the lab's upper limit is 0.49). A raised D-dimer does not mean you have a clot. It just means a clot can't be ruled out yet, so doctors follow it with a scan. That's the scan you remember: a CT angiogram of the chest (a CT scan with dye, done to look for a clot in the lungs) that same evening. The final report says: "No pulmonary embolism. Lungs are clear. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine."

Nothing else in your records points to a clot either. A pulmonary embolism is not on your list of conditions, which has only type 2 diabetes. And you have never been prescribed a blood thinner: your medicines are atorvastatin and Jardiance, and earlier metformin. If you'd had a clot, you would almost certainly have been put on one.

A few things the records don't tell us. They don't say why you were checked that day; the reason for the test or any visit notes aren't in your records. D-dimer can be raised by many harmless things, such as a recent infection, an injury or simply age. The "mild degenerative changes" in your upper back are common wear-and-tear and were a side finding, not related to a clot. If you have new chest pain, sudden breathlessness, or a swollen, painful leg, get seen urgently. A clear scan in 2025 doesn't rule out a new problem.
short: CT pulmonary angiogram on 2025-07-08 (done after a raised D-dimer of 0.92 mg/L FEU) was final: no pulmonary embolism, lungs clear. No PE diagnosis and no anticoagulant appear anywhere in my records.
